U1: Drawn from the running containers and the real wiring: every subnet is a bridge, and the LB, HAProxy and R2 share the 10.0.2.0/24 bridge. Red means a stopped container, amber means the container runs but the LB has marked the backend DOWN. Bars show each backend's share of requests.
U2: 10.0.1.1 is R1 (client side), 10.0.2.2 is R2 (LB side) and 10.0.3.11 is b1. Two router hops prove the traffic is routed, not bridged.
U3: Configured delay comes from topo/.netem_state, measured delay from a live ping c1 to the LB. They should agree within a few percent. Loss is applied in each direction, so a 5 % setting loses about 9.8 % of ping round trips.
U4: X-Backend-Id shows which backend served the request, and Connection: keep-alive shows the client leg stays open.
U5: The capture sends 3 requests on one connection. One SYN for 3 requests proves keep-alive on the client leg. Each forwarded request opens its own connection to a backend and carries X-Forwarded-For. Health probes appear about once per second per backend.
U6: Requests per second is computed by the relay from /stats counter deltas once per second. Percentiles come from the LB's own bounded sample of the last 100000 requests.
U7: Round robin gives equal shares, least-conn favours the fast backends, IP-hash keeps a client on one backend. Switch the algorithm in U13 and run load to see the shares move.
U8: Detection time is the first backend_down for b3 after the kill timestamp. A killed container answers with a TCP reset, so the LB sees 'refused' and needs 3 failed probes, about 3 s. A real host failure would time out.
U9: HAProxy statistics give counters, status and an average response time only. p50/p95/p99 are not invented. The shares are compared with the own LB's shares.
U10: Unequal capacity by design: delays 5/10/25/50 ms and CPU limits 1.0/1.0/0.5/0.25 from backends/.env. 'Live' is the limit read from the running container.
U11: Charted values come only from scripted run files. The checkpoint-2 files are one dry run per system and are labelled as such.
U12: CPU limits are read from the running containers (CpuQuota). Older environment.txt files wrongly said 'unlimited', so those lines are not shown.
U13: Fixed demo actions only. The relay runs a short list of known commands and accepts no command text from the browser. Own LB algorithm changes need the lab started with bash ui/start.sh.
U14: Every source reports when it last answered. Green is fresh, amber is stale, pink is offline.
